When processing input from EXT-PEER-P2P-BEACON, the system must ensure block must not be accepted into fork choice store without passing all checks..

All data crossing the trust boundary from EXT-EXECUTION-ENGINE-VIA-ENGINE-API to Consensus Layer (CL) must be validated according to: CL must handle EL responses defensively. A false is_inclusion_list_satisfied response could allow censoring proposers to bypass inclusion list enforcement. EL payload validity must be cross-checked.

All data crossing the trust boundary from EXT-CL-VIA-ENGINE-API to Execution Layer (EL) must be validated according to: EL must validate RANDAO value range (>2^64 confirms PoS context), withdrawal sequence constraints (max 16, ordered by index), and payload structural integrity. JWT authentication required but content validation essential.

All data crossing the trust boundary from EXT-IL-COMMITTEE-MEMBER-P2P to Consensus Layer (CL) must be validated according to: Must validate: committee membership, BLS signature, timing (before VIEW_FREEZE_CUTOFF at 75% of slot), transaction content validity. Late inclusion lists must be rejected.

All data crossing the trust boundary from EXT-USER-VIA-JSON-RPC to Execution Layer (EL) must be validated according to: Full parameter validation: mutual exclusion of transaction/hash parameters, standard transaction validation if tx provided, resource limits on subscription count/duration. Privacy consideration: node operators can observe monitoring patterns.

All data crossing the trust boundary from EXT-SMART-CONTRACT-CALLER to Execution Layer (EL) must be validated according to: Address range resolution must correctly distinguish EIP vs RIP precompile spaces. No address collision between ranges. On L1, calls to RIP range addresses should behave as calls to empty accounts.

All data crossing the trust boundary from EXT-BLOCK-PROPOSER-VALIDATOR to Consensus Layer (CL) must be validated according to: Proposer can bias RANDAO by 1 bit through selective withholding (forfeiting rewards). System accepts this as known limitation. Applications using PREVRANDAO must implement commit-reveal with multi-epoch delays. RANDAO value is propagated to EL via mixHash.

All data crossing the trust boundary from EXT-VALIDATOR-OPERATOR-EXIT to Consensus Layer (CL) must be validated according to: Signature must be verified against fixed Capella fork domain (CAPELLA_FORK_VERSION). Cross-fork replay is acceptable by design. Exits only initiate exit process, no fund transfer. Post-EIP-7044, exits signed with non-Capella domains must be rejected.

All data crossing the trust boundary from EXT-PROMETHEUS-SCRAPER to Execution Layer (EL) must be validated according to: Endpoint should be network-restricted to authorized monitoring systems only. Exposed metrics (sync status, peer count, block height) provide operational intelligence that could aid attack timing. No authentication mechanism defined in EIP-2159.

All data crossing the trust boundary from EXT-MALICIOUS-PEER-P2P to Execution Layer (EL) must be validated according to: All blocks and transactions from P2P must be fully validated. Eclipse attack mitigations required. Invalid data must be rejected without corrupting local state.

All data crossing the trust boundary from EXT-MALICIOUS-VALIDATOR-P2P to Consensus Layer (CL) must be validated according to: All proposals and attestations must be validated against consensus rules. Conflicting attestations trigger slashing. Censorship attempts mitigated by inclusion list enforcement (EIP-7805).

All data crossing the trust boundary from EXT-MEV-BOOST-RELAY to Consensus Layer (CL) must be validated according to: Relay-provided blocks must be fully validated. Relay data is untrusted. Particularly relevant with Gloas builder registry: builders onboarded via deposits must be verified through withdrawal credential classification and prior-signature checks to prevent unauthorized builder registration.

Despite specification ambiguity regarding 'The specification states merge transition block conditions are deleted but does not explicitly state...', the system must maintain consistent behavior by assume that pre-merge blocks are inherently invalid during capella since the merge is complete. any block without an execution payload would fail validation at an earlier stage..

Despite specification ambiguity regarding 'The withdrawals field in PayloadAttributes uses 'Sequence[Withdrawal]' without specifying maximum le...', the system must maintain consistent behavior by assume withdrawals sequence follows the same constraints as defined in the beacon chain capella spec (max 16 withdrawals per payload, ordered by withdrawal index)..

The system assumes The proof-of-stake merge has already completed before the Capella fork activates.. Violation of this assumption could result in: removing merge transition verification could allow invalid blocks that reference non-existent execution payloads to be accepted into the fork choice..

The system assumes The execution engine correctly processes the withdrawals field in PayloadAttributes and returns valid execution payloads.. Violation of this assumption could result in: if the execution engine ignores or misprocesses withdrawals, validators could miss withdrawal operations, locking user funds indefinitely..

Despite specification ambiguity regarding 'The specification does not clarify what happens if an EIP attempts to use an address in the RIP-rese...', the system must maintain consistent behavior by assume that eip process will enforce the reservation by rejecting eips that propose precompiles in 0x100-0x1ff. this is a governance assumption..

Despite specification ambiguity regarding 'The term 'RIP process' is used without a clear definition of what constitutes a valid RIP....', the system must maintain consistent behavior by assume rip refers to the rollup improvement proposal process as defined by l2 ecosystem governance, analogous to eip for l1..

The system assumes Assumes that L2 rollups will respect the reserved range and not deploy conflicting precompiles within their own address spaces.. Violation of this assumption could result in: multiple l2s could deploy different precompiles at the same rip address, causing cross-rollup interoperability issues..

The system assumes Assumes 256 addresses (0x100-0x1ff) will be sufficient for all RIP precompile needs.. Violation of this assumption could result in: future rip proposals may exceed available address space, requiring additional reservations or address reuse..

Despite specification ambiguity regarding 'Blocks previously validated as satisfying the inclusion list constraints SHOULD NOT be invalidated e...', the system must maintain consistent behavior by assume once a block passes il satisfaction check, the result is cached permanently in the store and never re-evaluated, even if the inclusion lists used for validation are later garbage collected..

Despite specification ambiguity regarding 'The conditions for proposer reorg ('shuffling stability, FFG competitiveness, finalization health') ...', the system must maintain consistent behavior by assume these conditions follow the existing proposer boost reorg logic from the base fork choice specification, extended to also require il satisfaction failure..

The system assumes The execution engine's is_inclusion_list_satisfied() function correctly determines whether a payload includes the required transactions.. Violation of this assumption could result in: a faulty or compromised execution engine could falsely report satisfaction, allowing censoring proposers to bypass inclusion list enforcement..

The system assumes Inclusion lists can propagate through the P2P network to all honest validators before the VIEW_FREEZE_CUTOFF (75% of slot).. Violation of this assumption could result in: late-arriving inclusion lists could cause honest validators to have inconsistent views, leading to disagreements on block validity and potential short-lived forks..

The system assumes A proposer cannot selectively withhold their block to avoid inclusion list enforcement while still receiving attestations.. Violation of this assumption could result in: strategic block withholding could allow proposers to censor transactions while maintaining chain weight through carefully timed late releases..

Despite specification ambiguity regarding 'The specification states monitoring continues if transaction 'not found in mempool' but doesn't clar...', the system must maintain consistent behavior by assume subscription remains active indefinitely until explicitly unsubscribed by client. implementations should document this behavior..

Despite specification ambiguity regarding 'No timeout or maximum subscription duration is specified for long-running subscriptions...', the system must maintain consistent behavior by assume implementations may define their own resource limits. clients should handle unexpected subscription termination..

Despite specification ambiguity regarding 'The exact definition of 'finality' is not specified - could mean different things on different chain...', the system must maintain consistent behavior by assume this refers to consensus-layer finality on pos chains. on chains without finality guarantees, this notification may never be sent or may use a confirmation count threshold..

The system assumes The Ethereum node maintains a mempool and can track transaction propagation. Violation of this assumption could result in: light clients or nodes without mempools may not be able to implement the full subscription behavior.

The system assumes Users trust the node to accurately report transaction inclusion and reorg events. Violation of this assumption could result in: malicious nodes could send false inclusion notifications, causing applications to act on unconfirmed transactions.

The system assumes Applications using reorg monitoring will implement appropriate logic to handle notifications. Violation of this assumption could result in: applications that don't handle reorg notifications may have inconsistent state or double-spend vulnerabilities.

The system assumes The notification mechanism provides transparency but does not prevent reorg-based attacks. Violation of this assumption could result in: users may assume monitoring provides protection when it only provides visibility.

All data crossing the trust boundary from EXT-PEER-P2P-BEACON to Consensus Layer (CL) must be validated according to: Full block validation required: ancestry verification, temporal validity (slot <= current slot), finalization constraints, state transition execution. Block must not be accepted into fork choice store without passing all checks.

All data crossing the trust boundary from EXT-EXECUTION-ENGINE-VIA-ENGINE-API to Consensus Layer (CL) must be validated according to: CL must handle EL responses defensively. A false is_inclusion_list_satisfied response could allow censoring proposers to bypass inclusion list enforcement. EL payload validity must be cross-checked.

All data crossing the trust boundary from EXT-CL-VIA-ENGINE-API to Execution Layer (EL) must be validated according to: EL must validate RANDAO value range (>2^64 confirms PoS context), withdrawal sequence constraints (max 16, ordered by index), and payload structural integrity. JWT authentication required but content validation essential.

All data crossing the trust boundary from EXT-IL-COMMITTEE-MEMBER-P2P to Consensus Layer (CL) must be validated according to: Must validate: committee membership, BLS signature, timing (before VIEW_FREEZE_CUTOFF at 75% of slot), transaction content validity. Late inclusion lists must be rejected.

All data crossing the trust boundary from EXT-USER-VIA-JSON-RPC to Execution Layer (EL) must be validated according to: Full parameter validation: mutual exclusion of transaction/hash parameters, standard transaction validation if tx provided, resource limits on subscription count/duration. Privacy consideration: node operators can observe monitoring patterns.

All data crossing the trust boundary from EXT-SMART-CONTRACT-CALLER to Execution Layer (EL) must be validated according to: Address range resolution must correctly distinguish EIP vs RIP precompile spaces. No address collision between ranges. On L1, calls to RIP range addresses should behave as calls to empty accounts.

All data crossing the trust boundary from EXT-BLOCK-PROPOSER-VALIDATOR to Consensus Layer (CL) must be validated according to: Proposer can bias RANDAO by 1 bit through selective withholding (forfeiting rewards). System accepts this as known limitation. Applications using PREVRANDAO must implement commit-reveal with multi-epoch delays. RANDAO value is propagated to EL via mixHash.

All data crossing the trust boundary from EXT-VALIDATOR-OPERATOR-EXIT to Consensus Layer (CL) must be validated according to: Signature must be verified against fixed Capella fork domain (CAPELLA_FORK_VERSION). Cross-fork replay is acceptable by design. Exits only initiate exit process, no fund transfer. Post-EIP-7044, exits signed with non-Capella domains must be rejected.

All data crossing the trust boundary from EXT-PROMETHEUS-SCRAPER to Execution Layer (EL) must be validated according to: Endpoint should be network-restricted to authorized monitoring systems only. Exposed metrics (sync status, peer count, block height) provide operational intelligence that could aid attack timing. No authentication mechanism defined in EIP-2159.

All data crossing the trust boundary from EXT-MALICIOUS-PEER-P2P to Execution Layer (EL) must be validated according to: All blocks and transactions from P2P must be fully validated. Eclipse attack mitigations required. Invalid data must be rejected without corrupting local state.

All data crossing the trust boundary from EXT-MALICIOUS-VALIDATOR-P2P to Consensus Layer (CL) must be validated according to: All proposals and attestations must be validated against consensus rules. Conflicting attestations trigger slashing. Censorship attempts mitigated by inclusion list enforcement (EIP-7805).

All data crossing the trust boundary from EXT-MEV-BOOST-RELAY to Consensus Layer (CL) must be validated according to: Relay-provided blocks must be fully validated. Relay data is untrusted. Particularly relevant with Gloas builder registry: builders onboarded via deposits must be verified through withdrawal credential classification and prior-signature checks to prevent unauthorized builder registration.

Despite specification ambiguity regarding 'The specification does not explicitly state what happens to exits signed with post-Capella fork doma...', the system must maintain consistent behavior by assume exits signed with non-capella domains will fail validation, as the signature verification now explicitly uses capella_fork_version..

Despite specification ambiguity regarding 'The phrase 'perpetually valid' could be interpreted as valid indefinitely in time, or valid across a...', the system must maintain consistent behavior by assume both interpretations apply: exits are valid across time (no expiration) and across forks (domain is fixed)..

The system assumes The withdrawal credential holder trusts that the validator operator will honor exit requests, as they cannot unilaterally force exits without the signing key.. Violation of this assumption could result in: withdrawal credential holders may be unable to exit their stake if operators refuse to sign exits..

The system assumes Downstream tooling (wallets, staking services) will be updated to use Capella domain for exit signing.. Violation of this assumption could result in: tools using current fork domain would produce invalid signatures..

The system assumes An attacker who obtains a signed voluntary exit cannot cause financial harm, only trigger the exit process.. Violation of this assumption could result in: if exits had additional effects (like slashing or fund transfer), this would be a critical vulnerability..
